newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran's parliament approves higher 1997/98 budget.
newsitem.headline: Iran's parliament approves higher 1997/98 budget.

text.p: Iran's parliament has approved a 188.6 trillion rial state budget for the Iranian year starting on March 21, projecting a 38 percent increase in both spending and revenue, Tehran radio said on Thursday.
It said deputies passed the annual budget in a late-night session on Wednesday.
Iran regularly predicts a balance between state income and spending in its annual budget, but some members of parliament say revenues are likely to fall short of the budget forecast.

The dollar value of the budget could range from $107.8 billion, if calculated at the official exchange rate used for essential state accounts, down to $62.9 billion at Iran's other official rate which the government appears to be using increasingly.

The budget increase is in line with an upward trend in recent years, which economists attribute to double-digit inflation, officially put at around 25 percent but estimated by some economists at up to 40 percent.
Income from oil exports -- Iran's main source of hard cash -- is budgeted at just over $17.5 billion at a price of $17.50 per barrel.
The current year's budget of 137.2 trillion rials is based on a price of $15.50 per barrel.

Iran, the world's third largest oil exporter, earned $2.67 billion above projections from oil exports in the first nine months of the current Iranian year because of high world petroleum prices, officials have said.

The budget law still needs final approval from the Guardian Council, a body of clerics and lawyers which vets parliamentary measures for conformity with Islam and the constitution. ($1=1,750 rials at the official rate used for essential state budget accounts such as oil and major national projects) ($1=3,000 rials at the official rate used in other cases)
